name: Strangers after 4 weeks' proximity: stimulus partner, 6 CCW fields, reversed (Persinger 2008)
origin: Persinger lab, Laurentian University (Persinger, Tsang, Booth & Koren 2008), circumcerebral 'Octopus' ring, paired-stranger design
summary: The stimulus partner's program from Persinger, Tsang, Booth & Koren 2008, in the reverse order given to half the pairs: six 5-min counter-clockwise ring configurations (three burst-firing, three Thomas) after the two strangers had met twice a week for four weeks. Persinger's lab reported more 5-6 Hz power over the temporal lobes of the unexposed partner in another room during the 20+2 frequency-modulated field (phase 3 here), in 4 pairs.
notes: Persinger & Lavallee 2010 confirm the design: 8 students drawn at random from a class roster of about 80, paid $50 per pair, meeting twice a week for 1 h over 4 weeks, then the sibling study's procedures with "20+2" fields; theta rose "more related to the temporal lobes, with a slight right hemispheric enhancement", and response partners reported a sensed presence, anger and sexual arousal. They add that strangers recruited off the street, with no shared history, showed no EEG or experiential change. The six configurations come from the 2008 paper's Table 1 as relayed secondhand (the paper itself could not be opened), so they are unverified (point duration, gap between pattern repeats, time on coil 1, change per coil): burst-firing 1 ms, 1 ms, 20 ms, +2; 1 ms, 2 ms, 100 ms, +20; 3 ms, 3 s, 200 ms, -2; frequency-modulated 1 ms, 1 ms, 20 ms, -2; 2 ms, 1 ms, 100 ms, +20; 3 ms, 3 s, 200 ms, -2. The signs are read literally, + longer and - shorter at each next coil: BF1 runs 20 to 34 ms (the papers' "20-2"), the +20 rows 100 to 240 ms, the 200-ms rows 200 to 186 ms and FM1, printed -2, 20 to 6 ms, the field the same paper's results call "20 ms (+2 ms)" and Persinger & Lavallee call "20+2". Persinger & Lavallee 2010 use "+" to mean shorter, which would give 20 to 6 ms for BF1, 20 to 34 ms for FM1 and 200 to 214 ms for the 200-ms rows; the literal reading was chosen because the +20 rows cannot shorten seven times from 100 ms, Cook 1999's full turns of about 200 to 2000 ms fit it better (216 ms per turn at 20 to 34 ms, 104 ms at 20 to 6 ms), and the Koren software patent (US 6,312,376) uses the plain sign. The schedule the lab actually ran was never published. Phase names give the actual time on each coil. The frequency-modulated rows are taken to be the lab's decelerating FM file, the Thomas pulse (Lehman 2016), played from the exact 849-point table; the burst-firing values were never published, so the built-in accelerating burst stands in (230 points; at 1 ms per point it plays three times faster, 18 to 90 Hz). This is the reverse-order half of the counterbalancing (FM3 to BF1); persinger-strangers-2008 runs the table order. These six fields are those of persinger-six-config-battery-2008 (the single-person Richards 2002 framing at 5 uT); this version runs at 1 uT, the paired studies' "1 microTesla range" (the 2008 table is relayed as 0.5 uT, with 1.5 uT measured 1 cm inside the ring and about 500 nT at its centre, all unverified), and adds the second person. Coil 1 left frontal, coil 8 right prefrontal, counter-clockwise from above (Persinger & Lavallee 2010): Fp1, FT7, TP7, O1, O2, TP8, FT8, Fp2 lie within 5 degrees of that 45-degree ring (the mapping Fp1, F7, T7, P7, Oz, P8, T8, Fp2 would leave only three coils on the right). Only the stimulus partner wears a helmet; both partners must know about and agree to the experiment. 4 pairs and many statistical tests; experiences were rated on an exit questionnaire that was not blinded, and anger or sexual arousal are reports that suggestion alone can produce; published in NeuroQuantology; never independently replicated. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Do not use results for decisions about real people. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on distress.
setting: Stimulus partner (this helmet): blindfolded, seated in a quiet, dark room (the lab used an acoustic chamber), imagining being with the partner, the instruction of the lab's sibling study. Response partner: another room, blindfolded with earplugs, no helmet, EEG recorded (the outcome measure); whoever scores the EEG should not know the phase times.
schedule: First the two meet twice a week for 1 h, within about 1 m of each other, for 4 weeks; then one 30-min session. For a self-test, add a session on the app's Blind option (real or sham at random) and score the EEG or the partner's reports before unblinding.
source: Persinger, Tsang, Booth & Koren 2008, Enhanced power within a predicted narrow band of theta activity during stimulation of another by circumcerebral weak magnetic fields after weekly spatial proximity: evidence for macroscopic quantum entanglement?, NeuroQuantology 6(1):7-21 https://doi.org/10.14704/nq.2008.6.1.151 ; Persinger & Lavallee 2010, Theoretical and experimental evidence of macroscopic entanglement between human brain activity and photon emissions, J Conscious Explor Res 1(7):785-807 (20+2 notation; coil 1 left frontal, coil 8 right prefrontal) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/99 ; Persinger, Koren & Tsang 2003, Percept Mot Skills 97:877-894 (sibling pairs) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14738355/ ; Lehman 2016, PhD thesis, Laurentian University ("20-2" = 20, 22 ... 34 ms) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/e7b03302-1b7f-4f4f-acf5-bdf41ee5370f/content ; Koren & Persinger, US 6,312,376 B1 (sequence interval and sequence acceleration) https://patents.google.com/patent/US6312376B1/en ; Thomas, Prato, Kavaliers & Persinger, US 6,234,953 B1, Table 1 (Thomas pulse point values) https://patents.google.com/patent/US6234953B1/en ; Buckner et al. 2015, PLoS ONE 10(4):e0124136 (Thomas file: 849 points at 3 ms) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/25875081 ; Carniello 2020, PhD thesis, Laurentian University (230-point burst-firing file) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/8c92763c-cd19-4a21-b242-3b572a28ce55 ; Booth, Koren & Persinger 2008, Electromagn Biol Med 27:426-436 (counter-clockwise vs clockwise) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19037792/ ; Cook, Koren & Persinger 1999, Neurosci Lett 268:61-64 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10400078/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1-6 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
